purpose: Exhibit one natural bounded-width CNF source family on which unsigned matching autarkies, sign-aware linear autarkies, and every fixed-degree Polynomial-Calculus/Macaulay refutation layer can all be simultaneously silent. The standard 3-colourability CNF is linearly lean for every graph by a four-clause local vertex argument, while published sparse-random graph families require linear Polynomial Calculus degree over every field.

standard_color3_cnf.variables: x_{v,1},x_{v,2},x_{v,3} for every graph vertex v.
standard_color3_cnf.vertex_at_most_one: For each color pair i<j, (NOT x_{v,i} OR NOT x_{v,j}).
standard_color3_cnf.edge_constraints: For every graph edge uv and color i, (NOT x_{u,i} OR NOT x_{v,i}).
standard_color3_cnf.equivalence: The CNF is satisfiable iff G is properly 3-colourable.

theorem_linear_leanness.name: EVERY_STANDARD_COLOR3_CNF_IS_LINEARLY_LEAN
proof: Fix one vertex v and write z_1,z_2,z_3 for the three linear-autarky coordinates of its colour variables.
The three negative pair clauses give z_1+z_2<=0, z_1+z_3<=0, z_2+z_3<=0.
Summing the pair inequalities gives 2(z_1+z_2+z_3)<=0, hence the sum is zero.
Then z_1=-(z_2+z_3)>=0, and similarly z_2,z_3>=0; with zero total all three coordinates are zero.
This holds independently at every vertex and does not use edge clauses. Therefore A z>=0 implies z=0 for the whole formula.
theorem_linear_leanness.matching_corollary: Linear leanness implies matching leanness because linear autarkies subsume matching-autarky reduction power. Thus the v4.6 and v4.7 kernels both delete nothing from this source family.

weights: Give the at-least-one clause of vertex v weight 2+deg(v).
Give each of its three at-most-one pair clauses weight 1.
explicit_positive_dual.balance: For each column x_{v,i}, the positive contribution is 2+deg(v); the two local pair clauses contribute -2 and the deg(v) incident edge-color clauses contribute -deg(v), so the total is zero.
explicit_positive_dual.consequence: This is an explicit y>0 with A^T y=0. The local four-row vertex block also has rank three, so the global matrix has full column rank, matching the v4.8 dual characterization.

polynomial_calculus_source_barrier.source_result: Conneryd, de Rezende, Nordstrom, Pang and Risse prove that sparse random regular graphs and sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs require Polynomial Calculus degree Omega(N) over every field to refute 3-colourability, with strongly exponential proof-size consequences.
polynomial_calculus_source_barrier.cnf_alignment: Their extended treatment explicitly states that the lower bound also applies to the standard CNF translation of graph colouring, not only to the compact polynomial presentation.
polynomial_calculus_source_barrier.consequence: For these unsatisfiable colorability formulas, no fixed-degree complete Macaulay/PC layer can refute the family. Reaching the necessary linear degree with the complete multilinear monomial basis is exponential by v4.4-v4.5.

combined_anti_loop.statement: There is one natural 3-CNF/2-CNF family for which matching-autarky reduction is silent, linear-autarky LP reduction is silent, and bounded-degree Polynomial Calculus/Macaulay closure is asymptotically incomplete.
combined_anti_loop.scope: This does not prove that every other polynomial preprocessor is silent on the same instances, and it is not a lower bound against arbitrary SAT algorithms. It specifically closes the hope that simply composing the v4.6/v4.7 autarky kernels with any fixed-degree version of v4.1 yields a universal polynomial decision procedure.

next_target.name: E8_COLOR3_RESIDUAL_NONPC_GLOBAL_INVARIANT_V5_0
next_target.directive: Use standard 3-colourability CNFs as a mandatory source-return benchmark. Any next universal candidate must make polynomial exact progress on linearly-lean colourability cores while not materializing linear-degree Macaulay state. Seek a non-PC global invariant, a polynomial-size high-degree sketch with exact zero-test, or a combinatorial minimax/contraction that exploits graph structure yet still extends back to arbitrary 3-SAT.

sources: Jonas Conneryd, Susanna F. de Rezende, Jakob Nordstrom, Shuo Pang, Kilian Risse, Graph Colouring Is Hard on Average for Polynomial Calculus and Nullstellensatz, FOCS 2023 / ECCC TR25-032.
Oliver Kullmann, Investigations on Autark Assignments, Discrete Applied Mathematics, 2000.
